title: Cap. 7 Theologi nostri: Vorstius — Amica duplic peculiar redemption sense
pass_a_gloss: Finally, lest I be tedious by heaping up more authors, Vorstius himself could not deny that the redemption accomplished on the cross pertains to the elect by a certain peculiar reason. For thus he speaks, in the Friendly Duplicate, page 230: It is agreed that the word redemption can be fitted in a diverse sense to several species of the same genus; and therefore that some only, and not all, can conveniently be said to have been redeemed by a certain special reason or peculiar sense, and are accustomed to be so called in the sacred writings. The same, page 235, answering the place brought from Hebrews 13:20, in which Christ is called the great Shepherd of the sheep through the blood of the eternal covenant, concedes to us that Christ is the Shepherd of these sheep, and indeed of these alone, in a peculiar manner, namely as to the saving and spiritual act of feeding them, which contains the actual donation of the Holy Spirit, and likewise as to a certain special acquisition of these sheep. Thus far he.
pass_b_english: Finally — not to weary by stacking more writers — even Vorstius could not deny that the redemption finished on the cross belongs to the elect in a peculiar sense. In the Friendly Duplicate (p. 230) he grants that redemption can be taken in different senses for several species of the same kind, so that some only, not all, may fitly be called redeemed in a special reason or peculiar sense, as Scripture often names them. On p. 235, answering Hebrews 13:20 (Christ the great Shepherd of the sheep through the blood of the eternal covenant), he concedes Christ is Shepherd of these sheep, and of these alone, in a peculiar way: as to the saving, spiritual act of feeding them (which includes the actual gift of the Holy Spirit), and as to a special acquisition of those sheep. So far Vorstius.
source_text: Denique, ne taedio sim plures autores congerendo, Vorstius ipse non potuit negare, redemtionem in cruce peractam peculiari quadam ratione ad electos pertinere. Sic enim loquitur, in Amica duplic. pag. 230, Constat redemtionis vocem diverso sensu ad plures ejusdem generis species aptari posse; ac proinde aliquos tantum, & non omnes, quadam speciali ratione seu peculiari sensu redemtos dici commode posse, inque sacris literis sic appellari solere. Idem, pag. 235. respondens loco adducto ex Heb. xiii. 20, in quo Christus magnus Pastor ovium per sanguinem foederis aeterni appellatur, concedit nobis, Christum esse harum ovium, & quidem harum tantum, Pastorem peculiari modo, puta quoad salvificam & spiritualem illas pascendi actum, qui actualem Spiritus sancti donationem continet, item quoad specialem quandam harum ovium acquisitionem. Hactenus ille.
